page_title: Learning to Fly: Let's simulate evolution in Rust (pt 4)

summary.title: Learning to Fly: Let's simulate evolution in Rust (pt 4)
summary.one_liner: You learn how to wire a Rust simulation of evolving birds into a browser via WebAssembly (wasm-pack, wasm-bindgen) and begin drawing the animals on a canvas.
keywords: how to draw on canvas from wasm
takeaways: Set up a Rust crate as a cdylib with wasm-bindgen and build it with wasm-pack, which generates JavaScript glue and a .wasm file.
Keep the simulation library frontend-agnostic and put a thin #[wasm_bindgen] wrapper crate on top of it.
Fix the getrandom 'target is not supported' error for wasm by enabling its js feature.
Expose data to JavaScript through wasm-bindgen structs and getters, using getter_with_clone for Vec fields.
Draw simulation state on an HTML canvas using a 2d context, fillStyle and fillRect.
summary.summary: The final part of the Learning to Fly series builds the world, animals and food for an evolution simulation in Rust, using nalgebra for points and rotations and rand for random initialization. It then creates a separate wasm-bindgen wrapper crate, compiles it with wasm-pack, and loads it into a JavaScript frontend scaffolded with npm init wasm-app and webpack. The author walks through the errors encountered along the way, such as the getrandom WebAssembly target issue and the Copy requirement for exposed fields. The page ends at the start of canvas drawing with fillStyle and fillRect, and the rest of the text is cut off before the animation is finished.
